subject: balloon
pitch: A hot-air balloon about to take off. A big envelope in bold vertical stripes of sunflower yellow, tomato red and sky blue with a patterned band around the middle, a burner glowing orange at the mouth, ropes down to a woven wicker basket with sandbags hanging on its sides and a little flag on one corner.
reasoning:
I'm planning out the TypeScript module structure using the builder API, deciding that since a balloon isn't a creature, I can mostly use plain parts rather than joints, with the envelope scaled to a realistic hot-air balloon size of around 15 meters tall.

I'm working through the model's scale: basket resting on the ground at y=0 with a height around 1.3m, a burner mouth above it around y=3.2m, and the envelope rising above that. I'm also considering how to add vertical stripes to the envelope using a lathe shape with a paint pattern.

Defining lathe profile points...

I'll simplify by skipping heavy smoothing and just marking the top and bottom rim corners as sharp, using around 16 segments for a clean low-poly look with smoothing level 1. I need to double check whether the lathe height values should be absolute or relative to the origin.

Writing paint function for diamond band pattern and vertical stripe sectors...

Writing band pattern logic...

Now I need the burner assembly: a steel-grey cylinder sitting in the mouth just above the basket, with an orange emissive flame shape glowing above it.

Actually I should lift the envelope mouth higher, say bottom at 4.0, so the burner can sit visibly from 3.4 to 4.0 just below the solid cap, pointing up at it with the flame glowing underneath.

I'm sketching the gap between the basket rim (ending ~1.4) and the envelope mouth (~4.0) — that leaves room for a simplified burner assembly. I'll place a grey steel cylinder burner around y 2.6–3.6 or a crown-ring shape near 2.9, treating it as stylized hardware suspended above the basket rather than literally accurate rigging.

I'm placing a grey cylinder burner housing topped by a glowing cone flame (orange outer, yellow core) that just reaches under the envelope mouth without clipping into it, then connecting the basket's corner points up to the skirt of the envelope with multiple thin ropes at calculated angles.

Now I'm shaping the basket itself using a tapered frustum box—narrower at the bottom, flaring out toward the lip—in a tan wicker tone, and considering adding a woven texture overlay to sell the material.

Positioning the basket cylinder so it spans y=0 to 1.0, with the rim sitting at the top. Now I'm thinking through how to support the burner above the basket, planning four vertical steel posts running from the rim corners up to the burner base.

For the sandbags, I'm sketching small burlap-colored shapes (tan, scaled spheres) hanging on the outside of the basket at a few points around its circumference, each with a darker tie at the top where it attaches to the rim, and working out their angular positions around the basket radius.

For the flag, I'm planning a pole rising from a corner of the basket rim up past the burner, with a triangular/curved flag shape extruded to face forward so it's visible from the front.

Checking the envelope mouth position and rope lengths from rim to skirt, then thinking through burner suspension and whether I need an explicit root joint—since createBuilder likely auto-creates one, with parts attaching to the nearest joint when no bone is specified.

I'll add a single root joint for clarity, confirming scenery parts can skip joints entirely. I'm also sketching the color palette for the envelope's painted band and sandbag geometry, scaling a sphere shape to get the right proportions.

Now I'm working out the burner assembly — positioning the steel housing box and connecting support rods from the basket rim up to the burner base, figuring out the right coordinates for each joint point.

For each of the 8 rim points on the basket, I'm placing them at matching angles so ropes stretch outward and upward to the skirt points, checking whether that many lines crossing the body still reads cleanly or if they'll clip through the basket itself.

Posts use the same rod approach with a steel color, and the envelope shape is built with a lathe using the paint color, defining the balloon outline with sharp corners at the skirt and smooth curves rising up through the envelope's widening and narrowing profile.

I'm considering whether to type-annotate the outline points array explicitly as OutlinePoint[] to avoid inference issues with mixed string/number tuples, and thinking through whether the lathe's crease detection will correctly keep the sharp corners at the base while smoothing the rest.

I'm also considering adding a decorative skirt band near the base of the envelope — a darker contrasting color where the rim meets the ropes — to give the balloon a more finished, designed look.

Now I'm working out the patterned mid-envelope band: a checkerboard alternating between cream and dark orange based on angular and vertical cell position, plus a separate sector-based striping scheme using three colors across 12 angular divisions. I'm writing the paint function that maps a point's height and angle to skirt, band, or envelope colors depending on which vertical zone it falls into.

For the basket weave texture, I'm sketching an SVG pattern of alternating rounded rectangles in greyscale strokes over a white background so it can be tinted by each part's actual color.

Minor overflow is fine since the basket cylinder wraps the texture once around, with four columns at 16 units covering the circumference at roughly 5cm per cell. The white fill will pick up a tan tint when multiplied against the wicker color, so I apply the weave texture as a textured part on the geometry.

Thinking through the cylinder geometry, I realize if it's open-ended, the far wall's interior would show its back face and get culled, making the basket interior look hollow through to the ground when viewed from above. To fix this I'll add a dark circular disc near the top, rotated flat to face upward, giving the illusion of an interior surface.

Still working out basket geometry...

Now I'm placing the rim torus and a darker bottom hoop for the wicker basket, then positioning three sandbags around the basket at scattered angles and scaled proportions to look draped over the edge.

Each bag connects to the rim with a thin rope cylinder, and I'm rotating the flattened sphere bags about the Y axis so their narrow face points radially outward from the basket center, matching their hanging position.

For the flag, I'm placing the pole at one of the rim corners (angle 45°, radius 0.6), running it from the rim height up to about y=2.1 — low enough to avoid clashing with the skirt ropes that also originate near that corner.

Now I'm working out the flag geometry itself: a wavy outline extruded with a small thickness, oriented so it faces the front and extends toward -X across the top of the basket. I need to get the orientation vectors right so the flag's visible face points outward toward the viewer rather than edge-on.

Then I'm positioning the pole, sizing the flag between y=1.7 and 2.0, picking a tomato-red color, and planning the support posts around the basket interior at radius 0.3, plus starting on the burner box geometry.

Now I'm sizing the burner box and posts, then building the burner pipe and flame cones — an outer orange cone with a yellow inner core stacked above the pipe, adjusting their vertical overlap so the flame base sits just above the pipe top. I'm considering adding a soft glow effect to make the flame look more luminous.

For colors, I'm setting the burner box and posts to a steel gray, the pipe to a lighter gray, and the ropes to a light tan. I'm placing eight skirt ropes radiating from the basket rim corners up to points near the balloon's bottom cap, making sure they attach visibly just below the lathe-generated flat cap surface so they read correctly from below, and deciding I don't need a ground plane since the model stands fine at y=0.

Now I'm centering the whole structure at the origin with the basket and burner aligned, aiming for roughly 19.6 meters tall and 10 meters wide to match a real hot-air balloon's proportions. I'm setting up the builder with a single import from the agentic-3js-builder package, defining a base joint at the origin, and keeping the part hierarchy simple since there's only one joint everything attaches to. I'm also preparing the meta export with the balloon's name and description, and laying out the core color palette for the envelope panels.

Writing lathe and rope code...

Adjusting the sandbag half-extents to a more realistic flattened shape, then building out the basket geometry: a tapered cylinder body with woven texture, torus rims at top and bottom for the rolled edges, and a circular disc inset for the interior floor. I'm working through the rotation math to make sure each piece faces the right direction after transforming from its default orientation.

Now I'm placing the burner assembly above the basket: three support rods angling outward, a steel burner box with a short connecting pipe, and layered flame cones (orange outer, yellow inner) sized so the inner flame stays nested inside the outer and the whole thing clears the balloon envelope's bottom opening with a small safety gap. I'm also adding a small flagpole and pennant off one side of the basket rim, working out the geometry so the flag drapes correctly in the right direction and color.

I'm defining the paint function for the balloon envelope: a dark skirt band near the bottom, a checkered cream/accent pattern in a mid-height band, and multicolor stripes elsewhere, using the surface's height and angle to decide which color each cell gets.

Now I'm shifting to generating a separate woven-pattern SVG icon, laying out rows of rounded white rectangles with gray strokes over a grey background to resemble a basket weave texture.
